title: Dennis Ritchie, Ken Thompson, and the Creation of C (1972-73)
explainer: Thompson and Ritchie built C at Bell Labs specifically so Unix's kernel and system software could be written in a portable language instead of hand-tuned assembly for each new machine; it grew out of Thompson's earlier language B, itself derived from BCPL. The choice to keep C close to the hardware - direct pointer arithmetic, no automatic bounds checking, data layouts that map straight onto memory - is why the language still functions as 'portable assembly' today, which is exactly the niche this lesson explores.
